summary: Root plays like a fable about power: each faction has a completely different rulebook and win condition, so the Marquise's engine-building race feels nothing like the Vagabond's solo questing or the Eyrie's rigid, self-punishing card program. Games are tense and swingy, with the leader getting dogpiled and board states shifting fast once someone starts scoring points.
praised: asymmetric factions that each feel like a different game
tight 60-90 minute playtime for its depth
criticised: steep teaching burden since every player needs to learn a different faction
brutal to newer players who don't understand threat assessment
runaway leader problem if the table doesn't gang up
Eyrie's forced moves can feel punishing

interaction.detail: All factions place and move pieces on one shared woodland map, battling to remove each other's warriors and seize control of clearings. Players also draw from a shared card deck, and because each faction is so different in power, informal negotiation and alliances between weaker players against a leader are common.

subsystems: faction-unique primary VP engine (Marquise: building construction; Eyrie: roost presence/Decree upkeep; Woodland Alliance: sympathy spread; Vagabond: quests and faction relationships)
universal secondary VP triggers (crafting items, removing enemy buildings/tokens)
sources: crafting items for their printed value
scoring.how_you_win: Each asymmetric faction races its own scoring engine (buildings, roosts, sympathy, or quests) plus shared crafting/battle points until someone hits 30 victory points and wins immediately; alternatively, a player holding an activated dominance card wins outright by completing that card's objective instead of chasing points.
scoring.score_note: ends at 30 VP; dominance/coalition wins skip score
